Tired of your AI coding assistant hallucinating spaghetti code, skipping tests, and derailing your architecture? 🛑

Meet Superpowers (https://github.com/obra/superpowers) — the framework that transforms unguided coding agents into disciplined engineering partners by injecting a structured SDLC, automated planning, and subagent-driven development directly into your favorite CLI and editor harnesses. 

Instead of letting LLMs instantly write unstructured code, Superpowers intercepts the workflow to enforce requirements brainstorming, architecture design, and production-grade engineering standards.

🔥 Key Features:

• Universal Plugin Support: Native integrations and skill bootstraps across major AI coding harnesses including Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and more.
• Autonomous Subagent-Driven Development: Dispatches fresh subagents for bite-sized engineering tasks, executing isolated coding loops with automated intermediate code reviews.
• Enforced TDD: Integrates strict Red-Green-Refactor practices that halt execution until a failing test is written, verified, and resolved.
• Isolated Git Worktrees: Automatically provisions clean workspaces on dedicated branches before implementation begins.

Scale up your AI agents from simple code completion tools into autonomous junior engineers capable of executing complex development plans reliably. Eliminate code review fatigue and lock down enterprise-grade quality control today.

What if you could run Xbox Series X and S games on Windows PCs without the massive performance overhead of full system CPU emulation? 🎮⚡

Enter XCL: a groundbreaking compatibility layer that enables console-exclusive titles to execute natively on Windows by letting game x64 code run straight on your PC processor. 

Traditional emulators struggle with heavy translation costs. XCL solves this by using a brilliant architectural approach:
👉 Native CPU execution for game binaries, avoiding CPU emulation overhead.
👉 RDNA2 shader bytecode re-compilation into HLSL and DXIL, executing seamlessly on standard PC GPUs via Direct3D 12.
👉 Independent re-implementations of Xbox GDK console system libraries like kernelx.dll and XGameRuntime.
👉 Comprehensive DirectStorage and texture decoding integration for BCPack and precise tiling layouts.
👉 Automated GPU testing pipelines that validate translated shaders instruction by instruction.

For systems programmers, graphics engine developers, and reverse engineers, this is an incredible architectural reference. Study how to handle PE loader data-driven import routing, shared CPU/GPU title memory windows, and direct machine code compatibility layers without breaking a sweat. 🛠️💻

Check out the repository and explore the source code today:
https://github.com/xcl-dev/xcl

🚀 What if you could run macOS natively on ARM64 Linux hardware—without a hypervisor?

Meet xnulinux: a mind-bending project that embeds Apple's open-source XNU kernel directly inside an unmodified Linux kernel as a loadable module. 

For years, running macOS apps on non-Apple hardware meant heavy virtualization overhead. xnulinux solves this by running XNU natively on Linux kernel threads pinned to CPU cores, letting standard macOS userspace apps like Safari, Chrome, and WindowServer execute right alongside Linux processes on the exact same CPUs and memory space.

🔥 Key Features:

⚡ Hypervisor-Free Execution: Powered by a foreign kernel interface module (fki.ko) that manages memory, timers, files, networks, and GPU access.
🎮 Hardware & GPU Acceleration: Uses a Vulkan-to-Metal translation layer via Mesa Venus and a custom DRM bridge (xnudrmd) to pass hardware acceleration directly to hosted macOS apps.
🧠 Physical Memory Management: Allocates a physically contiguous memory block from Linux using CMA and maps it with XNU's native pmap using 4K pages.
🖥️ Full Desktop Stack: Boots a stock macOS system disk to a fully functional desktop environment including launchd, Finder, Dock, and networking.

Whether you are an advanced systems programmer, a kernel hacker, or an infrastructure engineer, this project is an extraordinary reference implementation for cross-kernel compatibility, custom machine layers, and hybrid kernel architectures. 

Run macOS build agents or CLI tools directly on bare-metal ARM64 Linux servers with zero virtualization overhead.

🎮 Ever wondered how to boot next-gen console builds natively on a standard Windows x86-64 desktop? 

Meet VIctory: an experimental, enthusiast-driven compatibility layer designed to load and execute console builds of modern AAA titles directly within its own Windows process space—bypassing traditional virtualization entirely! 🚀

For systems programmers, low-level graphics engineers, and emulator architects, this repository is a goldmine for studying advanced runtime design. 

Here is what makes VIctory stand out:
⚡ Native Process Execution: Runs original x86-64 console binaries inside a custom Windows process while supplying missing platform services and APIs.
🔄 Advanced Shader Translation: Performs ahead-of-time and on-the-fly shader translation from console GPU bytecode to host DirectX Intermediate Language (DXIL) with configurable caching.
📂 High-Performance Storage: Implements parallel archive reading, data decoding, and tiled texture management matching the source platform storage model.
🕹️ Seamless Input & Upscaling: Translates standard XInput gamepads or keyboard layouts directly, complete with an integrated Series S mode using AMD FidelityFX upscaling.

Whether you want to analyze how complex console architectures map to desktop D3D12 hardware, study proprietary asset parsing, or explore high-performance systems architecture in Rust, you need to check this out.

🔗 Explore the repository and dive into the source code here: https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory
